root_cause.text: In `net/bridge/br_arp_nd_proxy.c`, `br_nd_send()` assumed the Neighbor Discovery options in `struct nd_msg *ns->opt[]` were already in the linear portion of the incoming skb, but its callers only guaranteed the ICMPv6 header and target address were present, so parsing `ns->opt[]` on a non-linear skb could read past the linear buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch message says “its callers only guarantee that the ICMPv6 header and target address are available, so the option area can still be non-linear,” and the fix adds `skb_linearize(request)` before option parsing plus recalculates `ns` from `skb_network_header(request)` after linearization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor `br_nd_send()` to make `ns` a local variable instead of a function parameter.
intent_record.what: The function `br_nd_send()` had its parameter list changed by removing the `struct nd_msg *ns` argument. Inside the function, a new local declaration `struct nd_msg *na, *ns;` was added, combining `na` and `ns` into one declaration. The previous separate declaration `struct nd_msg *na;` was removed.
intent_record.how: This changes `ns` from being supplied by the caller to being obtained or assigned within `br_nd_send()` itself, while preserving the existing local use of both `na` and `ns` in the function body. Runtime behavior is only affected insofar as the function no longer depends on an external `ns` argument.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add skb linearization failure handling in bridge neighbor discovery send path to avoid processing non-linear packets.
intent_record.what: In `br_nd_send()`, the single null-device check `if (!dev)` was changed to a combined check `if (!dev || skb_linearize(request))`, causing the function to return early not only when `dev` is null but also when `skb_linearize(request)` fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now ensures the `request` skb is linearized before continuing. If linearization fails, neighbor discovery packet construction and transmission are aborted, preventing later code from operating on a non-linear skb that may not be safely accessed in the existing logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the ND message pointer from the request skb so neighbor discovery processing uses the correct packet payload.
intent_record.what: A new assignment initializes `ns` to point to the Neighbor Discovery message in the received `request` skb by computing `skb_network_header(request) + sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)` and casting it to `struct nd_msg *`.
intent_record.how: This makes the code explicitly reference the IPv6 ND payload in the incoming packet before later option processing, ensuring `ns` points at the correct message contents instead of relying on an uninitialized or previously set value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust br_do_suppress_nd() to match the updated br_nd_send() interface by removing the obsolete msg argument from its call sites.
intent_record.what: The calls to br_nd_send() in br_do_suppress_nd() were updated to remove the final msg argument: one call for VLAN-tagged packets now passes skb->vlan_proto and skb_vlan_tag_get(skb) only, and the non-VLAN case now passes 0 and 0 only.
intent_record.how: This changes the br_nd_send() invocation signature at the call site, so the function is no longer provided the msg parameter from these two branches. Runtime behavior depends on the updated br_nd_send() definition, but the visible effect is that these ND suppression send paths now use the reduced argument list and no longer supply an extra message value.

relevance_review.reason: The change is a refactor that only makes `ns` a local variable in `br_nd_send()`. It does not address the root cause of unsafe parsing of ND options from a potentially non-linear skb or add any bounds/linearization checks.

The change directly addresses the root cause by handling non-linear skb cases in the bridge neighbor discovery send path, preventing unsafe parsing of Neighbor Discovery options beyond the linear buffer.

The change targets neighbor discovery packet handling in br_arp_nd_proxy.c and specifically adjusts how the ND message pointer is initialized from the request skb. That is directly related to the root cause, which was unsafe parsing of ND options from an skb whose linear data was not guaranteed to contain them.

This change only updates call sites to match a revised br_nd_send() interface by removing an obsolete argument. It does not address the root cause of the bug, which was unsafe parsing of Neighbor Discovery options from a possibly non-linear skb.

candidates.rationale: This comment marks the code region where Neighbor Discovery options are assumed to be available for processing; the vulnerable logic in this path proceeds to parse beyond the guaranteed linear header area on non-linear skbs.

This length computation begins the option-parsing path based on the request skb, and it is part of the pre-fix logic that proceeds without first ensuring the skb is linearized, enabling out-of-bounds reads when options reside outside the linear buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the start of the Neighbor Discovery option-length calculation in br_nd_send(). In the vulnerable pre-fix logic, this path proceeds to parse ND options from the request skb without first guaranteeing the skb is linear, which can lead to reading past the linear buffer on non-linear skbs.

This comment marks the exact code region where option parsing begins. The root cause is in this processing path: the function assumes ND options are safely accessible in the linear area of the skb, but callers only guaranteed the ICMPv6 header and target address.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
bridge: suppress nd pkts on BR_NEIGH_SUPPRESS ports

This patch avoids flooding and proxies ndisc packets
for BR_NEIGH_S
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit ed842faeb2bd49256f00485402f3113205f91d30
Author: Roopa Prabhu <roopa@cumulusnetworks.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 6 22:12:39 2017 -0700

    bridge: suppress nd pkts on BR_NEIGH_SUPPRESS ports
    
    This patch avoids flooding and proxies ndisc packets
    for BR_NEIGH_SUPPRESS ports.
    
    Signed-off-by: Roopa Prabhu <roopa@cumulusnetworks.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/bridge/br_arp_nd_proxy.c b/net/bridge/br_arp_nd_proxy.c
index a79c1824e16
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in br_nd_send(). The function comments and code show it assumes it can read Neighbor Discovery options directly from the skb linear data: `ns_olen = request->len - (skb_network_offset(request) + sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)) - sizeof(*ns);` followed by `for (i = 0; i < ns_olen - 1; i += (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3)) { ... }`. This parses `ns->opt[]` without first ensuring the options are actually present in the linear portion, matching the root cause. The only header safety check shown is in br_is_nd_neigh_msg(), which uses `skb_header_pointer()` for `sizeof(*msg)` at the ICMPv6/target header, but br_nd_send() still dereferences `ns->opt[]` directly and contains no extra linearization or safe option access. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet applied in this snippet.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `br_nd_send()` contains the vulnerable construct: it directly iterates over `ns->opt[]` using `ns->opt[i]` and `ns->opt[i + 1]` without first ensuring those Neighbor Discovery options are in the linear part of the skb. The risky code is: `ns_olen = request->len - (skb_network_offset(request) + sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)) - sizeof(*ns); for (i = 0; i < ns_olen - 1; i += (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3)) { if (ns->opt[i] == ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR) { daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr); ... } }`. The root cause says callers only guaranteed the ICMPv6 header and target address were present, so reading `ns->opt[]` on a non-linear skb could access beyond the linear buffer; this code still assumes direct access to `ns->opt[]`. There is no fix here such as using `skb_header_pointer()`/`skb_copy_bits()` for the options or validating linearity before parsing, so `is_fixed` is false.
